newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FEAR AND GREED TO KEEP BRUSSELS BOURSE VOLATILE.
newsitem.headline: FEAR AND GREED TO KEEP BRUSSELS BOURSE VOLATILE.

text.p: Investors gripped both by fear and greed will continue to spark jerking movements of the Bel-20 index .BFX in the next trading sessions, analysts said.
"It gives an indication of the degree of nervousness in the market," said Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co.
"It's fear and greed at the same time...people know the index has gone up so much and that it can all go wrong now. And yet they don't want to miss out on any further gains," he said.
The Bel-20 was more than 2.5 percent lower shortly before U.S. retail sales and PPI data were issued, but recovered after the release to stand 0.46 percent lower at 2,440.67 by 1317 GMT.

Players had been worried the data US-ECI would have come in strong and stoked U.S. inflation and rate rise worries. But the reports on inflation and retail sales were favourable and also helped the dollar recover against the mark. The greenback was earlier hurt by an inflation warning from the Bundesbank.

Casteleyn said the same see-saw scenario might repeat itself as early as Thursday, when a new raft of U.S. data, including key July CPI, are due. The market is closed on Friday for Assumption. The Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday is the market's next target.
"I'm expecting a few more nervous days," Casteleyn said.
Analysts said the Bel-20's downward correction was a healthy interlude and just a prelude to renewed buying interest.
"The fundamentals are still good, there is no inflation. There will probably be no major correction," Casteleyn said.
He did not expect the Federal Reserve nor the Bundesbank to hike rates next week.
The basic trendline for the next few months, however, could be rather flat with ups and downs scattered around.
Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen noted that the slide earlier on Wednesday again showed how vulnerable the market was.
"It will also fend off questions from investors asking why we were not fully invested and were still holding on to our cash position," De Mesure said.

Casteleyn said the Bel-20 had been less erratic on Wednesday than the Dutch AEX index .AEX. The Amsterdam index had peaked only last week, compared with the Bel-20 which had reached its high two weeks ago and had already been slipping before today.
Analysts said individual features or shares were of lesser importance on key data days.
"People are more playing the market now," Casteleyn said.
